subject.title: Policy plugins cannot see resolved/served model identity at any blocking-capable hook (security impact: our confidentiality guard failed open)

question: Which public plugin API shape should carry resolved provider/model identity for pre-submission policy enforcement?
rationale: The narrow source bug is clear on the CLI path, but the permanent contract affects third-party plugins, provider routing, and a reported confidentiality boundary, so maintainers should choose the supported shape before implementation.

options.title: Standardize existing context contract
options.body: Guarantee ctx.modelProviderId and ctx.modelId on before_agent_run across embedded and CLI agent paths, document it as read-only policy input, and add regression tests.

options.title: Add a new post-resolve blocking hook
options.body: Introduce a dedicated pre-model-call hook, which is more explicit but broadens the plugin SDK and needs compatibility/API review.

options.title: Split provider hook exposure into design work
options.body: Fix before_agent_run identity now and keep before_provider_request/after_provider_response exposure as a separate provider-hook design discussion.

recommendation.title: Standardize existing context contract
recommendation.body: Guarantee ctx.modelProviderId and ctx.modelId on before_agent_run across embedded and CLI agent paths, document it as read-only policy input, and add regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent CLI hook-context and agent-core harness history make vincentkoc the best routing candidate for the immediate contract decision.
